title: Bear and Chase
statementMd:
Bearland has $*n*$ cities, numbered $1$ through $*n*$. There are $*m*$ bidirectional roads. The $*i*$-th road connects two distinct cities $*a*_{*i*}$ and $*b*_{*i*}$. No two roads connect the same pair of cities. It's possible to get from any city to any other city (using one or more roads).

The distance between cities $*a*$ and $*b*$ is defined as the minimum number of roads used to travel between $*a*$ and $*b*$.

Limak is a grizzly bear. He is a criminal and your task is to catch him, or at least to try to catch him. You have only two days (today and tomorrow) and after that Limak is going to hide forever.

Your main weapon is BCD (Bear Criminal Detector). Where you are in some city, you can use BCD and it tells you the distance between you and a city where Limak currently is. Unfortunately, BCD can be used only once a day.

You don't know much about Limak's current location. You assume that he is in one of $*n*$ cities, chosen uniformly at random (each city with probability ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e89669ce77a802a91e3fecccc124a73dd0007895.png)). You decided for the following plan:

1. Choose one city and use BCD there.
- After using BCD you can try to catch Limak (but maybe it isn't a good idea). In this case you choose one city and check it. You win if Limak is there. Otherwise, Limak becomes more careful and you will never catch him (you loose).
2. Wait $24$ hours to use BCD again. You know that Limak will change his location during that time. In detail, he will choose uniformly at random one of roads from his initial city, and he will use the chosen road, going to some other city.
3. Tomorrow, you will again choose one city and use BCD there.
4. Finally, you will try to catch Limak. You will choose one city and check it. You will win if Limak is there, and loose otherwise.

Each time when you choose one of cities, you can choose any of $*n*$ cities. Let's say it isn't a problem for you to quickly get somewhere.

What is the probability of finding Limak, if you behave optimally?

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 400$, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/57d4722e24aa597aa7a64ac80642a700052e744b.png)) — the number of cities and the number of roads, respectively.

Then, $*m*$ lines follow. The $*i*$-th of them contains two integers $*a*_{*i*}$ and $*b*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $*a*_{*i*} ≠ *b*_{*i*}$) — cities connected by the $*i*$-th road.

No two roads connect the same pair of cities. It's possible to get from any city to any other city.

## Output

Print one real number — the probability of finding Limak, if you behave optimally. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute error does not exceed $10^{ - 6}$.

Namely: let's assume that your answer is $*a*$, and the answer of the jury is $*b*$. The checker program will consider your answer correct if $|*a* - *b*| ≤ 10^{ - 6}$.

## Note

In the first sample test, there are three cities and there is a road between every pair of cities. Let's analyze one of optimal scenarios.

1. Use BCD in city $1$.
- With probability ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/64c94d13eeb330b494061e86538db66574ad0f7d.png) Limak is in this city and BCD tells you that the distance is $0$. You should try to catch him now and you win for sure.
  - With probability ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/14b21b617fcd2e25700376368355f7bbf975d8de.png) the distance is $1$ because Limak is in city $2$ or city $3$. In this case you should wait for the second day.
2. You wait and Limak moves to some other city.
- There is probability ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png) that Limak was in city $2$ and then went to city $3$.
  - ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png) that he went from $2$ to $1$.
  - ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png) that he went from $3$ to $2$.
  - ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png) that he went from $3$ to $1$.
3. Use BCD again in city $1$ (though it's allowed to use it in some other city).
- If the distance is $0$ then you're sure Limak is in this city (you win).
  - If the distance is $1$ then Limak is in city $2$ or city $3$. Then you should guess that he is in city $2$ (guessing city $3$ would be fine too).

You loose only if Limak was in city $2$ first and then he moved to city $3$. The probability of loosing is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/55bd5cf64609940bba840be4d13d882b3b49c511.png). The answer is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/56d7c14b8db6605aa95b947bca89a66828b49171.png).
statementZhMd:
Bearland 有 $*n*$ 个城市，编号从 $1$ 到 $*n*$。有 $*m*$ 条双向道路。第 $*i*$ 条道路连接两个不同的城市 $*a*_{*i*}$ 和 $*b*_{*i*}$。不存在两条道路连接同一对城市。任意两个城市之间都可以通过一条或多条道路互相到达。

城市 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$ 之间的距离定义为从 $*a*$ 到 $*b*$ 所需经过的最少道路数。

Limak 是一只灰熊。他是一个罪犯，你的任务是抓住他，或者至少尝试抓住他。你只有两天时间（今天和明天），之后 Limak 就会永远躲起来。

你的主要武器是 BCD（熊型罪犯探测器）。当你位于某个城市时，你可以使用 BCD，它会告诉你你所在城市与 Limak 当前所在城市之间的距离。不幸的是，BCD 每天只能使用一次。

你对 Limak 当前所在的位置知之甚少。你假设他均匀随机地位于 $*n*$ 个城市中的某一个（每个城市的概率为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e89669ce77a802a91e3fecccc124a73dd0007895.png)）。于是你决定采取以下计划：

1. 选择一个城市并在那里使用 BCD。
- 使用 BCD 后，你可以尝试抓捕 Limak（但这可能不是个好主意）。此时你选择一个城市并进行检查。如果 Limak 在那里，你就获胜。否则，Limak 会变得更加谨慎，你将永远无法抓住他（你会失败）。
2. 等待 $24$ 小时，以便第二天再次使用 BCD。你知道 Limak 会在这段时间内改变位置。具体来说，他会从自己的初始城市出发，等概率地选择一条道路，并沿着这条道路前往另一个城市。
3. 第二天，你再次选择一个城市并在那里使用 BCD。
4. 最后，你尝试抓捕 Limak。你选择一个城市并进行检查。如果 Limak 在那里，你就获胜，否则失败。

每次选择城市时，你都可以选择任意一个 $*n*$ 个城市。可以认为你能够迅速到达任意地点。

如果你采取最优策略，找到 Limak 的概率是多少？

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 400$，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/57d4722e24aa597aa7a64ac80642a700052e744b.png)）——城市数和道路数。

接下来有 $*m*$ 行。第 $*i*$ 行包含两个整数 $*a*_{*i*}$ 和 $*b*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*a*_{*i*}$ ≠ $*b*_{*i*}$）——第 $*i*$ 条道路所连接的两个城市。

不存在两条道路连接同一对城市。任意两个城市之间都可以互相到达。

## 输出格式

输出一个实数——如果采取最优策略，找到 Limak 的概率。如果你的答案与标准答案的绝对误差不超过 $10^{ - 6}$，则会被判定为正确。

具体来说，假设你的答案为 $*a*$，评测程序的答案为 $*b*$。当且仅当 $|*a* - *b*| ≤ 10^{ - 6}$ 时，评测程序会认为你的答案正确。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，有三个城市，且每一对城市之间都有一条道路。下面分析一种最优方案。

1. 在城市 $1$ 使用 BCD。
- 以 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/64c94d13eeb330b494061e86538db66574ad0f7d.png) 的概率，Limak 位于该城市，BCD 会告诉你距离为 $0$。此时你应该立即尝试抓住他，并且一定会成功。
  - 以 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/14b21b617fcd2e25700376368355f7bbf975d8de.png) 的概率，距离为 $1$，因为 Limak 位于城市 $2$ 或城市 $3$。此时你应该等待第二天。
2. 你等待了一段时间，Limak 移动到了另一个城市。
- Limak 起初位于城市 $2$，之后前往城市 $3$ 的概率为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png)。
  - 他从 $2$ 前往 $1$ 的概率为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png)。
  - 他从 $3$ 前往 $2$ 的概率为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png)。
  - 他从 $3$ 前往 $1$ 的概率为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/45372faa18afd6691c4e5aa94c7b5edc43a23007.png)。
3. 再次在城市 $1$ 使用 BCD（当然，也可以选择在其他城市使用）。
- 如果距离为 $0$，那么你可以确定 Limak 在这个城市中（你获胜）。
  - 如果距离为 $1$，那么 Limak 位于城市 $2$ 或城市 $3$。此时你应该猜测他位于城市 $2$（猜测城市 $3$ 也可以）。

只有当 Limak 起初位于城市 $2$，之后移动到城市 $3$ 时，你才会失败。失败的概率为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/55bd5cf64609940bba840be4d13d882b3b49c511.png)。答案为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/56d7c14b8db6605aa95b947bca89a66828b49171.png)。
